title: Conveyor: Efficient Tool-aware LLM Serving with Tool Partial Execution
technique: Tool partial execution: start executing a tool while the LLM is still decoding its plan, via a tool-developer interface and partial-execution-aware scheduler

optimized_metrics.evidence: We build Conveyor, an LLM serving system that enables tool partial execution to significantly reduce the total request completion latency
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: We run each workload 100 times and collect the average latency

headline_claim.text: tool partial execution can improve request completion latency by up to 38.8%

reported_metrics.where: Fig 6 (average request completion latency, 100 runs, error bars)
Fig 8 theoretical vs empirical latency improvement

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Without tool partial execution, the total execution time is Lold = sum_{i=1..n} (g_i + t_i) + g_{n+1}.
metric_definitions.notes: Latency of one tool-assisted request = sum over rounds of LLM generation time g_i (prefill+decode) and tool time t_i, incl. final decode; best case sum max{g_i,t_i}+g_{n+1}. This is a multi-round (program-like) completion time per request, single-request, no queueing.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: with a corresponding relative latency improvement given by (sum (g_i+t_i)+g_{n+1}) / (sum max{g_i,t_i}+g_{n+1}) - 1
metric_definitions.notes: Improvement is defined as old/new - 1, so the Validation workload's '376.4%' is a ratio-based speedup, not a percentage reduction; abstract's 38.8% is the same definition.

load_regime: single request run 100 times per workload (average latency and std); no load sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: Improvement depends heavily on tool characteristics; not all workloads benefit equally (Validation 376.4% from early abort).
hardware: 2x NVIDIA RTX 3090 (2x Xeon Gold 5215), PyTorch + FlashInfer
models: not stated in the sections read (LLM served in PyTorch implementation)
workloads: Six constructed tool scenarios: CodeGen, Search, Planning, Validation, etc.
extractor_notes: Abstract's '38.8%' is a ratio-defined improvement (old/new - 1), so the 376.4% figure appears in the text with the same definition. Evaluated one request at a time: no throughput, TTFT or tail metrics. Request completion latency here spans multiple LLM-tool rounds, i.e. PROGRAM_JCT-like.
